## Forecasts you can compare with the published prices

The price-series and retail-price sensors now expose `raw_forecast_reference`.
Home Assistant keeps the first forecast received for each future slot. Later
forecasts and official day-ahead prices do not overwrite it. A new ApexCharts
example draws official prices, the current forecast and the saved reference
as three separate lines.

- Snapshots survive Home Assistant restarts and remain until the target
  market day ends. There is no unlimited historical archive.
- Collection starts with this update. Past forecasts cannot be reconstructed.
- `captured_at` identifies the local observation time, not the model run time.
  This is a visual comparison, not a fixed-lead-time quality measurement.
- Market and retail snapshots stay separate. Switching currency, settlement
  resolution or retail formula starts a new compatible comparison.
- No additional API requests, credentials or recorder configuration are needed.
  Existing entities, automations and planning inputs remain unchanged.
- The chart preserves zero and negative prices, draws complete intervals and
  leaves missing data as gaps rather than filling them with invented prices.

## Choose your contract's settlement interval

This release also includes the previously prepared choice between hourly and
quarter-hourly settlement. Select the interval your supplier actually bills;
price requests and local state changes follow that choice. The default remains
quarter-hourly, preserving existing configurations.

## Updating

Update Energy Price Forecast EU in HACS and restart Home Assistant. For the
comparison chart, also install ApexCharts Card 2.1.0 or newer and use
`examples/price-chart-comparison.yaml`, replacing all three entity placeholders
with your price-series or retail-price sensor. Adjust the axis unit to match
that sensor. An empty saved-reference line immediately after updating is normal.

Validation: 365 Python tests and four tests executing the chart's actual
JavaScript generators pass. A visual check on a real dashboard is still
recommended; no live Home Assistant installation was used for that check.
